classification.difficultyReason: The first two parts explicitly scaffold complementary-angle tangent expressions; combine the two perpendicular ground distances using Pythagoras.

content.prompt: Two landmarks $P$ and $Q$ on level ground are observed from the top $T$ of a vertical tower $BT$ of height 30 m. Landmark $P$ is due south of the tower, while landmark $Q$ is due east of the tower. The angles of elevation of $T$ from $P$ and $Q$ are $15^\circ$ and $18^\circ$ respectively.

spec.description: Spatial tower diagram with solid PT, TQ and PQ, dashed PB, BQ and BT, perpendicular marks at B, and highlighted elevation angles.
spec.mathematics: BT is perpendicular to the horizontal plane and is 30 m. PB is perpendicular to BQ. Angle BPT is 15 degrees and angle BQT is 18 degrees.

sizing.exceptionReason: The narrow elevation sectors require native 10 pt labels clear of both rays. The 65 mm figure preserves all givens and the viewing direction without reducing type size.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find, correct to the nearest metre, the distance between the two landmarks.

answer.worked:
$PB\perp BQ$ because the landmarks are due south and due east of the tower.

$$\begin{aligned}PQ&=\sqrt{BP^2+BQ^2}\\PQ&=\sqrt{(30\tan75^\circ)^2+(30\tan72^\circ)^2}\\PQ&\approx145\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$
